question: When presenting her second term of office1, Ursula von der Leyen made reference to the 146page report by former Italian Prime Minister Enrico Letta. Beyond auto-enrolment clauses for Europeans’ bank deposits in financial funds2, this report presents worrying threats to democracy in Europe.

Letta calls for the division of powers between Brussels and the Member States to be ignored3 and for national competence to be rejected in areas such as health4. He also calls for a ‘Permanent Citizens’ Conference’ to be set up (who will elect them?), referring only to Article 114 of the Treaty5, and a ‘Transatlantic Single Market’ to be established (who will decide if we want more sugar or more GMOs?)6.

He nostalgically refers to the Commission’s 2018 plan to allow border residents to choose the national legislation that applies to them. Finally, he suggests that the Commission should withdraw its legislative proposals when MEPs and governments decide on a different text that ‘would threaten the single market’. 1.
How much in total has Enrico Letta been paid in allowances/remuneration for his 400 meetings7 in Europe?
Why did the Commission select an expert in tourism, Eric Philippart, as sherpa (senior expert) to support this report?
How many grants have been awarded to the various institutes and experts called upon for this report?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.4.2025) Following on a call by the European Council, the Spanish government, the Belgian government, and the Commission have asked Mr Enrico Letta to write an independent HighLevel Report on the future of the Single Market in 20231. The Commission did not conclude a contract with Mr Letta and did not pay him any allowances or remuneration.

The Commission did not award grants to institutes or experts specifically for this report. The Senior Expert in the Directorate-General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs, was seconded from November 2023 to June 2024 at the request of the Belgian government, to support the work on the independent High-Level Report on the future of the Single Market.
The Belgian presidency of the Council selected him on the basis of his academic and professional experience on Single Market policies and Better Regulation.
1 See also the Commission’s press release of 15 September 2023, IP/23/4495.
